candidates.exact_span: Monitoring and reporting requirements begin on the effective date of this permit. Compliance with the Whole Effluent Toxicity limitations is required on Permit Effective Date.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Effective-date language governs when WET limits become enforceable and when monitoring obligations start; different readings of permit effective date or compliance start date change FY2025 applicability and limit timing.

candidates.exact_span: See PART II, Whole Effluent Toxicity Testing Requirements for additional WET monitoring and reporting conditions.

candidates.exact_span: Once per permit term. The test is to be performed during the first springtime after the permit effective date, during the irrigation season when irrigation return flows in the lower Animas Ditch likely discharge back to the Animas River when most sensitive juvenile life forms are likely to be present in the receiving water and colder ambient temperatures might adversely affect treatment processes.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The seasonal, site-specific, and biological timing window is highly interpretive; different readings of when the single required test must occur change whether monitoring was required in FY2025 and how absent results should be classified.

candidates.exact_span: This permit does not establish requirements to automatically increase the WET testing frequency after a test failure, or to begin a toxicity reduction evaluation (TRE) in the event of multiple test failures.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Explicit negation of automatic retest/TRE frequency obligations affects whether additional post-failure monitoring was required versus discretionary agency follow-up.

candidates.exact_span: upon failure of any WET test, the permittee must report the test results to EPA and NMED, Surface Water Quality Bureau, in writing, within 5 business days of notification the test failure.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Failure-triggered reporting within 5 business days is a distinct monitoring/reporting obligation whose applicability and timing depend on interpreting 'failure' and 'notification' events.

candidates.exact_span: EPA and NMED will review the test results and determine the appropriate action necessary, if any.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Agency discretion after failure affects whether follow-up monitoring or TRE becomes required versus remaining unresolved; this changes classification of missing post-failure evidence and ongoing obligations.
